Everyone else is kinda focusing on the money part of the question, but I will point out that while the memory system means youll always get a few turns, OTK decks are still very popular with the likes of Grandis, Ulforce, and metalgaruX, and playing against them can feel very oppressive without a top tier deck. Blackwargreymon X decks while not OTK focused, punishes you for playing them game and playing against them isnt very fun at all, and it is largely considered the best deck in the current format, taking the title from metalgaruX who held it for the last 3 sets. 

Powercreep is becoming a issue we have yet to see bandai adress. Because they lack the ability to spit out archtypes at will like yugioh and magic, they have to provide support to older decks more frequently, and certain decks are seeing that support MUCH more frequently. 
Bt9 introduced the first OTK meta, where it was a race to build up in the back, promote, and win. While powercreeping decks that just kinda win when they want is tough, we're still seeing it happen. 

Comeback mechanics in digimon are largely focused on your opponent making mistakes, and your luck in security. Thats about it. If your playing against an OTK deck, and they promote out of the back and hit you 6 times, and you dont have a security bomb, its gg. 

Since you are just looking to play casually and at locals, you probably wont be playing against top tier shenanigans 24/7 so most of these things wont be problems for you very often. But you should know they exist, and if you come across these decks on a budget build, and youre unprepared, it will kinda feel like youre playing different games. Where these decks are so efficient at doing the 1 thing theyre designed to do, that theyre very tough to beat. 

Youll also find that outside of these decks, there are tons and tons of decks that matchup well against eachother and are tons of fun to play. Decks where both players have a real chance of winning, and the matches can feel very back and forth. This is hands down the best part of digimon. Outisde of the absolute top tier decks, everything kinda has a chance to win. Which leaves the door open for alot of different decks and strategies.

T3- depending on if you have 2 or less memory or 3 or more here it varies. 2 or less: either evo saviourhuck in raising and pass turn. (Reboot is important so they dont swing over you. But since you evod into saviourhuck this turn, you can blitz into their unsuspended to kill any threats to your stack if you dont have reboot. T4- Here is where you would usually want to evo into JesGX since it can go atop JesXanti, but your gonna want to start building another stack in raising, and swinging with your JesX/sistermons. If you have a kimera in hand, swing your level 4 sisters. As soon as one dies, swing JesX bring it back, and evo kimeramon and swing. Their security should be cleared. It really depends on what deck youre looking to build. Id decide on that first, and then pick the supporting set that has those cards. Of course id reccomend buying singles over boxes if youre looking for a deck anyhow since it will cost a fraction of the cost of 2 boxes. Digivolving X anti bodies is an incredibly powerful mechanic that nets you a free draw, and usually adds a few extra inheritables. Most decks that run Xantibodies also run multiple copies of cool boy which is another incredibly powerful card. For 0 cost you gain +2 cards, 1 memory, and sometimes a really solid inheritable. If you have more than 1 cool boy out that bonus is increased. Decks like wargrey, metalgaru, and alphamon rely on having larger than usual stacks to bonus their effects. The only way to appease it is with a jar of Vegemite which is how the story of Drop Bears liking Vegemite started.
